description: No dedicated public procurement profile page was located for Česká exportní banka (ČEB) or for ČSSZ within this run's searches; results returned other entities instead.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced Česká pošta, EGAP and Národní rozvojová banka profiles but not ČEB/ČSSZ profiles. This is unresolved, not proof of absence — both are almost certainly mandatory contracting authorities and should be resolvable by IČO lookup in VVZ's profile registry.

why_it_matters: ČEB is a state bank and ČSSZ runs mass benefit payment flows; both are high-value buyers of payment infrastructure. Missing them would be a real evidence gap.

description: No page was fetched directly in this run; all candidates come from search-result evidence only.

result.result_summary: URLs and IDs are reported as discovered, not as verified-live. Several of these portals (NEN, VVZ, smlouvy.gov.cz) are known to be session/JS-heavy and may return 403 or empty shells to naive fetchers.

why_it_matters: Liveness and crawlability must be established by the deterministic verification pass before collection design is finalised.

description: Commercial banks (ČSOB, KB, Česká spořitelna, Air Bank, Moneta) are NOT contracting authorities for most of their IT, so their core-banking/card vendor choices do not appear in this cell's sources at all.

result.result_summary: This cell can only evidence the public/state-owned slice: ČNB, NRB, ČEB/EGAP, Česká pošta, ministries, ČSSZ, municipalities.

why_it_matters: Prevents over-claiming market share from procurement data alone; commercial-bank vendor mapping needs other workstreams (vendor press releases, annual reports, ČNB registers).

description: No Czech-language term set was established for 'core banking system' as used in Czech tender titles.

result.result_summary: Searches for 'core banking' in cs returned no distinctive local phrasing; Czech tenders appear to use English-in-local ('core banking') or descriptive phrases such as 'bankovní informační systém'. Not confirmed against real notices in this run.

why_it_matters: Keyword recall on NEN/VVZ/Registr smluv will be poor until the actual Czech title conventions are harvested from real award notices.

description: Neither the English nor the Czech seed query surfaced an actual TED contract-award notice for a Czech banking-software contract under CPV 72212443, or for an ATM services supplier in CZ. General web search returns TED explainer/scraper marketing pages, not notices.

result.result_summary: TED notice content is effectively invisible to general web search engines; only one real notice URL (ted.europa.eu/cs/notice/465605-2025/pdfs) surfaced incidentally, via the Czech-language query.

why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell CANNOT be worked by web search. Collection must go through TED's own search/API/bulk XML. Any pipeline design that assumes search-engine discoverability of notices will silently under-collect.

description: Czech-language queries containing 'platební terminály' and 'bankomaty' are dominated by retail/commercial content — bank product FAQs (Česká spořitelna Platbomat, ČSOB, Global Payments), accounting-software help pages, and terminal resellers.

result.result_summary: Majority of cs results were vendor marketing, not procurement documents.

why_it_matters: These are noisy terms. Czech procurement queries must be anchored with procedural vocabulary ('zadávací řízení', 'nadlimitní veřejná zakázka', 'profil zadavatele', 'oznámení o výsledku') or restricted to the procurement domains, or precision collapses.

description: No EU-funded programme or project specifically dedicated to Czech PAYMENTS infrastructure was identified. NPO/OP TAK/DIGITAL material describes digitalisation of public administration, healthcare, justice and building permits, plus generic business digitalisation — payments appears only implicitly (e-government payment gateways, digital identity).

result.result_summary: Searched cs and en; found funding envelopes and digital pillars but no payments-specific programme line.

why_it_matters: The 'EU-funded digitalisation programmes touching payments' half of this cell is thinner than assumed. Payments exposure has to be found bottom-up from individual tenders/beneficiaries rather than top-down from a programme line.

description: An authoritative CPV code-browser URL could not be confirmed; SIMAP content appears to have been folded into ted.europa.eu/en/simap. The candidate entry uses the inferred simap.ted.europa.eu/cpv URL with reduced confidence.

result.result_summary: No direct search hit for a canonical CPV browser page.

why_it_matters: The CPV whitelist is the backbone of every query in this cell; the canonical code list must be located and pinned before building the pipeline.

description: NIPEZ documentation indicates the original Czech open-data series covers procurement recorded in the Věstník and on e-marketplaces only through January 2024, after which the new Registr veřejných zakázek applies.

result.result_summary: A documented discontinuity in the Czech national open-data series around Jan 2024.

why_it_matters: Time-series analysis of vendor win-share across that boundary will be misleading unless both the legacy and new datasets are ingested and reconciled. TED is the more continuous spine for above-threshold contracts.

description: No live fetch of TED search result pages, the TED API, or E-ZAK/NEN listings was performed in this pass; all findings rest on search-engine evidence and official documentation pages.

result.result_summary: URLs are provided with confidence scores but no liveness claim, per the run's rules.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must check especially the inferred URLs (simap CPV, celnisprava section index, isvz.nipez.cz/opendata) rather than the well-attested ones.

description: The public part of the Czech beneficial ownership register (Evidence skutečných majitelů, esm.justice.cz) was made inaccessible to the public by the Ministry of Justice effective 17 December 2025, citing Supreme Court, Supreme Administrative Court and CJEU case law on disproportionate interference with privacy.

result.result_summary: ESM can no longer be used as an open ownership-unmasking source; access is limited to the entity itself via data box, privileged public authorities, AML-obliged persons on request, or parties proving legitimate interest to a court.

why_it_matters: This removes the single most direct route to identifying who really stands behind a CZ fintech or PSP; ownership analysis must fall back on shareholder entries in the obchodní rejstřík, Sbírka listin filings, LEI Level-2 parent data and foreign parent registers, all of which are less complete.

description: The 2024 amendment to the Czech transformations act removed the duty to publish paid notices about merger/transformation projects and creditor notices in the Obchodní věstník; the projekt přeměny and creditor notices are now deposited in the Sbírka listin at least one month before approval.

result.result_summary: M&A event detection has shifted from a searchable gazette feed to per-company document filings.

why_it_matters: A monitoring pipeline built only on Obchodní věstník will silently miss vendor mergers and acquisitions from 2024 onward; watchlist-driven Sbírka listin polling is now required.

description: No dedicated, publicly documented open-data dataset was found that extracts structured financial statement line items (revenue, EBITDA) from Sbírka listin PDFs for CZ companies; filings appear to be published as documents (often scans) rather than as structured XBRL-style data.

result.result_summary: Financial extraction from Czech statutory filings requires document download plus OCR/parsing, or a paid credit-bureau layer (CRIBIS, Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet-type providers).

why_it_matters: Cost and latency of the workstream's financial-evidence pipeline are materially higher than in jurisdictions with structured filing data; budget for OCR or a commercial licence.

description: Both ARES and the credit-bureau aggregators impose usage limits or licence conditions: MF ČR reserves the right to restrict users exceeding roughly 500 queries per minute or performing random-data automated crawling of ARES, and CRIBIS-type services are contractual databases that forbid bulk extraction.

result.result_summary: Automated collection must be rate-limited and, for commercial profiles, licence-based rather than scraped.

why_it_matters: Ignoring these terms risks IP blocks on the single most important entity-resolution service for the whole CZ workstream.

description: German Unternehmensregister/Bundesanzeiger and some ČNB JERRS application endpoints were not fetched in this pass; their URLs are recorded from search results and prior knowledge, not from a successful retrieval.

result.result_summary: Treated as unverified rather than dead; liveness is to be established by the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents false 'dead source' records for portals that are typically session-driven or bot-defended.

description: No active, well-maintained Czech association dedicated specifically to non-bank payment institutions / PSPs with a public member list was confirmed. ASPPS ČR (aspps.eu, IČO 04387783) exists in the commercial register and describes an advocacy role, but its web presence looks minimal (plain http, .eu domain) and no member list was observed.

result.result_summary: ASPPS ČR identified as the only candidate; membership depth unverified. In practice the PSP population is covered by Česká fintech asociace rather than a dedicated PSP body.

why_it_matters: Means there is no single association-side census of Czech payment institutions; the ČNB licence register must carry that load, with ČEFTAS as the commercial-signal overlay.

description: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) appears under two domains (bankovnikarty.cz and bankovni-karty.cz) with legacy static-HTML page structures and no recent activity surfaced in search.

result.result_summary: Statutes and a 'činnost a členové' page were indexed, but currency could not be established in this pass. Recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: SBK was historically the coordination venue for Czech card payments and card-market statistics; if dormant, that coordination has migrated to ČBA commissions and the schemes themselves, which changes where card-market intelligence should be collected.

description: APEK operates a members-only zone (apek.cz/prihlaseni) behind which richer member data and materials likely sit; only the public alphabetical member list is openly enumerable.

result.result_summary: Public list is collectable; the member zone is out of scope and should not be accessed.

why_it_matters: The 580+ merchant enumeration remains usable, but any member-only vendor briefings or benchmark data are not legitimately collectable and should not be assumed available.

description: Searches surfaced association member and working-group directories but no association-hosted case-study or reference-implementation library for banking/payments technology in CZ.

result.result_summary: Associations publish position papers, rulebooks and statistics rather than vendor case studies; the closest substitutes found are ČBA scheme rulebooks and conference/PDF archives (e.g. ICT UNIE assembly minutes, ČBA presentations hosted on university sites).

why_it_matters: The 'case studies' topic for this cell must be served indirectly — via association event programmes and member presentations — rather than by a directory. Another cell (vendor websites / conferences) should own it.

description: The Czech Banking Association is reachable under at least two domains — cbaonline.cz (current site, member list and working groups) and czech-ba.cz (the domain the ČNB index still links, with its own /cs/o-cba/komise-pracovni-organy path).

result.result_summary: Both appear live in search results; which is canonical was not established.

why_it_matters: A collector pinned to the wrong host risks silent staleness or duplicate records for the same association; the canonical host must be resolved before scheduling recurring collection.

description: No official award-programme domain for Zlatá koruna was confirmed during this pass; every result returned was syndicated press coverage (penize.cz, kurzy.cz, bankovnictvionline.cz, czechbanking.cz, profipf.cz, moneta.cz) rather than the organiser's own site.

result.result_summary: Zlatá koruna is recorded as an indirect (PR-cluster) source pending resolution of its canonical domain. It is NOT assumed dead — only unverified.

why_it_matters: The organiser site would carry the full category tables, jury composition and multi-year archive that the press releases only summarise; without it, longitudinal award analysis depends on fragile third-party coverage.

description: The seed-adjacent term 'Zlatý měšec' returned no matching CZ award; searches redirected to 'Zlatá koruna' and to Měšec.cz (a consumer finance portal). The Czech-language query was run explicitly and did surface local results, just not the hypothesised award.

result.result_summary: No evidence found in this pass that a currently-active award named 'Zlatý měšec' exists; treat the name as a noisy/possibly-defunct term rather than a source.

why_it_matters: Prevents a future run from burning queries on a non-existent programme, and flags 'měšec' as a noisy token that collides with the Měšec.cz brand.

description: No CZ event branded 'Banking Summit CZ' (as listed in the cell brief) was located in either Czech or English searching. The functional equivalents found are IT ve finančnictví, FIN (R)Evoluce, CARDFORUM and the new Fintech Week CEE.

result.result_summary: 'Banking Summit CZ' recorded as unconfirmed; possibly a generic descriptor rather than a brand, or a renamed/discontinued event.

why_it_matters: Avoids a phantom source entry and redirects effort to the events that actually carry CZ bank + vendor line-ups.

description: No public exhibitor or sponsor roster was located for a Czech bank-run hackathon; Komerční banka's hackathon was documented only through a dated trade-press article, and no 2025 CZ bank hackathon results page surfaced in Czech-language search.

result.result_summary: Bank hackathon outputs (winning teams, partner tooling, mentor employers) appear to be published sporadically via PR rather than on stable pages.

why_it_matters: Hackathon winner and mentor lists are exactly the pre-press-release partnership signal the cell exists to capture; the absence of stable pages means this signal must be caught via press monitoring, not crawling.

description: Seamless Europe's most reliable index in this pass was its LinkedIn company page; the canonical event domain was not confirmed and LinkedIn requires authentication for full browsing.

result.result_summary: Exhibitor roster reachable in principle (200 exhibitors reported) but not via an unauthenticated, confirmed URL yet.

why_it_matters: One of the two international delegation targets named in the cell brief currently lacks a crawlable entry point.

description: Money20/20 Europe attendee-level intelligence is available chiefly through commercial resellers (Landbase, Vendelux) rather than the organiser; the organiser publishes sponsors but not a full attendee list.

result.result_summary: Sponsor directory is free and usable; attendee lists are a paid third-party product with unclear provenance.

why_it_matters: Sets expectations that CZ-delegation-level detail at international shows cannot be obtained free and reliably, and that reseller lists should not be treated as authoritative.

description: Czech-language queries targeting jobs.cz/prace.cz for vendor product names (Temenos, Mambu, Finastra) returned no actual CZ job listings; the general web index surfaced only US/UK aggregators (ZipRecruiter, ITJobsWatch).

result.result_summary: No individual CZ vacancy naming a core-banking vendor was retrieved via general web search in this pass.

why_it_matters: The highest-value signal in this cell (a Prague ad requiring Temenos/Mambu experience) is not reachable through general search engines; it requires querying the job boards' own site search directly.

description: LinkedIn job search and employee skill profiles — the richest source for this cell — are behind an auth wall and their ToS forbids automated collection; search engines returned only public company landing pages.

result.result_summary: No CZ-filtered LinkedIn results obtainable; source recorded as blocked/manual-only.

why_it_matters: Employee skill profiles are often the only public proof that a bank runs a given platform; losing automated access forces manual analyst effort and slows detection.

description: No dedicated engineering blog was found for Komerční banka, ČSOB, Raiffeisenbank CZ, MONETA or Air Bank; only Česká spořitelna operates a public tech-community portal (ittrendy.cz).

result.result_summary: Bank tech-blog coverage in CZ is effectively a single-source category.

why_it_matters: Weak-signal collection for the other banks must lean harder on job ads, API docs and GitHub, since they publish no engineering narrative.

description: No Czech-language RFP-adjacent contractor/body-shop listing site specific to banking IT was identified in this pass; searches surfaced only generic IT job boards (easy-prace.cz, jenprace.cz, dobraprace.cz).

result.result_summary: Contractor/subcontractor-listing sub-category unresolved.

why_it_matters: Subcontractor and freelance listings often name the end client's platform explicitly and would be a distinct early-warning channel.

description: No Printec Czech Republic careers page or CZ job listing was found; only Diebold Nixdorf (Prague, Plzeň) and NCR Atleos global careers surfaced.

result.result_summary: Printec CZ hiring footprint unconfirmed in this pass.

why_it_matters: Absence of local hiring artefacts for a self-service/ATM vendor is itself a competitive-footprint signal, but needs confirmation rather than inference from a single search.

description: No Czech-specific Downdetector-equivalent outage archive with historical, queryable data was located. Searches surfaced only journalistic write-ups of outages (Deník, Peníze.cz, aRecenze) rather than a structured status/outage dataset for CZ banks, gateways or card schemes.

result.result_summary: Downdetector CZ country pages were not confirmed in results; outage evidence is currently only narrative press coverage plus, presumably, individual bank status pages not yet enumerated.

why_it_matters: Outage frequency/duration per institution is one of the strongest demand-side quality signals for this cell; without a structured feed the workstream must reconstruct timelines from press, which is slower and biased toward large incidents.

description: Public operator pages for DPP/PID contactless fare payment describe terminal counts and the DOS/XT-Card carrier ecosystem but do not name the acquirer, terminal supplier or payment processor behind the open-loop card acceptance.

result.result_summary: Search explicitly returned that no concrete supplier for the in-vehicle contactless acceptance was identified in operator or PID materials.

why_it_matters: Vendor attribution for the flagship CZ transit deployment is missing, so acquirer/terminal-vendor market-share inference in transport is currently unsupported from buy-side sources alone.

description: APEK's flagship E-commerce Study (payment-method mix) is free only to association members; non-members face a purchase barrier.

result.result_summary: APEK announcement page states the 2025 study is free for members; full datasets are not openly downloadable.

why_it_matters: The best quantitative payment-mix time series for CZ e-commerce cannot be collected by crawling and needs a licensing/membership decision.

description: Merchant-side disclosure for Notino and Košík of their payment providers was not found; only Alza (Adyen) and Rohlík (Adyen listed among online-payment services, plus crypto work with Confirmo) yielded provider-level evidence in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searches on Notino/Košík payment providers returned no primary or trade-press provider attribution.

why_it_matters: Leaves gaps in the top-merchant PSP map that this cell is supposed to build; requires checkout-level technical fingerprinting or subprocessor/privacy-policy inspection instead of search.

description: For consumer outage-tracking platforms there is no established Czech-language term or local service; searches had to rely on the English brand 'Downdetector' plus cs terms 'výpadek'/'nedostupnost'.

result.result_summary: cs terms 'výpadek', 'odstávka', 'nedostupnost' work for press coverage but no local crowd-outage platform exists in results.

why_it_matters: Documents that local-language coverage for this sub-topic is inherently limited, not an omission by the scout.

description: No ČNB open-data CSV dataset specifically for payment institutions / e-money institutions / small-scale payment service providers was confirmed on the Otevřená data page. The datasets observed were banks and foreign bank branches (p_seznam=1), money changers (2), credit intermediaries (3, and further categories) and non-bank consumer credit providers (7).

result.result_summary: Payments-sector entities appear to be reachable via JERRS and possibly WS JERRS, but a dedicated bulk open-data export for platební instituce was not evidenced in the fetched page content.

why_it_matters: The payments register is the backbone of this cell; if no bulk export exists, collection needs either the certificate-gated WS JERRS API or careful scraping of JERRS, which materially changes the effort estimate.

description: WS JERRS web services require authentication with a commercial certificate from eIdentity, I.CA, PostSignum or an EU trust-list CA.

result.result_summary: The official API is not anonymously accessible; this is documented policy rather than a fetch failure.

why_it_matters: Any plan assuming a free public API over the ČNB register is wrong; budget for certificate procurement or design around open data / scraping.

description: The DORA 'registr informací' (register of ICT third-party providers and contractual arrangements) submitted annually by each financial entity to ČNB is a supervisory reporting artefact, not a published register.

result.result_summary: Only ČNB's templates, webinar decks and reporting guidance are public; the actual bank-to-vendor mappings are confidential.

why_it_matters: This would be the single most valuable vendor-relationship dataset in the CZ market if it were public. It is not — vendor mapping must be reconstructed from procurement, enforcement decisions, and company disclosures instead.

description: No settled Czech-language term or dedicated regulator page was found for 'case study' / vendor reference project in a supervisory context; searches in cs surfaced only 'stanoviska', 'rozhodnutí' and 'zprávy'.

result.result_summary: Case-study material from the regulator side exists only implicitly, embedded in enforcement decisions, arbitrator findings and supervision reports.

why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect a regulator-published case-study source in CZ; case studies must be mined from decision texts or sought in vendor/press cells.

description: No ČNB-published list of pending/ongoing licence applications (a forward-looking pipeline of prospective payment institutions) was found in either cs or en searching.

result.result_summary: Only the licensing process description and the register of granted authorisations were located.

why_it_matters: New-entrant detection will therefore be lagging (visible only on licence grant) unless supplemented by media, funding and trade-register sources.

description: No engineering/technology blog owned by any of the eleven target CZ banks was found. Searches in Czech for 'technologický blog', 'blog pro vývojáře', 'engineering blog' plus bank names returned only consumer media and comparison sites, no bank-hosted tech blog and no bank Medium publication.

result.result_summary: Zero owned tech-blog sources identified for ČS, KB, ČSOB, Moneta, RB, UniCredit CZ, Air Bank, Fio, Creditas, Trinity, Partners Banka.

why_it_matters: Tech blogs are usually the richest owned source of vendor/stack detail. Their apparent absence means vendor intelligence for CZ must lean on IR/annual reports and vendor-side case studies instead.

description: No owned-channel announcement was found in which Air Bank, Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS or Partners Banka names its core-banking system vendor. Czech-language queries combining bank names with 'core banking systém', 'dodavatel' and 'tisková zpráva' returned only third-party profiles and aggregator directories.

result.result_summary: Core-banking vendor for the four challenger/small banks is undisclosed on their own channels as far as this pass could see.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale only partially: challengers do not self-disclose core vendors the way KB did. Vendor-side channels (cell for vendor press rooms) will have to carry this.

description: Landing-page URLs for several owned document hubs were inferred from observed PDF paths and site structure rather than seen directly: KB výsledky hospodaření hub, Air Bank výroční zprávy page, UniCredit Bank CZ výroční zprávy page, Banka CREDITAS 'pro média' page, Fio 'o nás' Czech path. The linked PDFs/subpages were observed in search results; the hub URLs were not.

result.result_summary: Five candidate source_url values are best-guess hub paths pending deterministic verification.

why_it_matters: A verification pass should resolve these to canonical hubs; a 404 here means 'moved', not 'absent', since the underlying documents demonstrably exist.

description: No dedicated ČSOB CZ press-room URL was surfaced in this pass; only a direct press-release PDF (tz250213.pdf under /documents/) and the mandatory-disclosure hub were observed. Czech query 'csob.cz pro média tiskové zprávy' did not return the press index itself.

result.result_summary: ČSOB press room exists in practice but its index URL was not observed.

why_it_matters: ČSOB is a top-3 CZ bank; missing its press index leaves a hole in owned-channel monitoring that must be closed by site navigation rather than search.

description: Bank-owned channels rarely name a vendor; the vendor's own channel does. The one clear CZ core-banking vendor disclosure (KB → Temenos Transact, implementation partners named as Syncordis and LTIMindtree) appeared on temenos.com, businesswire and trade press, while KB's own IR text describes the programme as 'nová digitální banka' without vendor branding.

result.result_summary: Owned bank channels give programme names, budgets and timelines; vendor channels give vendor names. The two must be joined.

why_it_matters: Sets the collection design: use bank IR/annual reports as the spine (dates, capex, programme names) and vendor press rooms as the attribution layer.

description: No Czech bank client could be identified for Mambu or Thought Machine from vendor-owned content. The nearest CEE reference is 365.bank (Slovakia) on Backbase + Mambu.

result.result_summary: Searches returned platform comparison pages and partner listings, not CZ deployments.

why_it_matters: Suggests next-gen cloud cores have little or no publicised CZ install base; CZ tier-1 modernisation is going to Temenos instead. Watch Slovakia/Poland as leading indicators.

description: Finastra, Tietoevry and BPC Banking Technologies produced no CZ-specific customer story or press release in search.

result.result_summary: Only generic product/corporate pages returned; no CZ bank named.

why_it_matters: Either genuine absence from CZ or references held privately; requires direct newsroom/case-study-library crawls rather than search-engine discovery before concluding absence.

description: No Comarch case study for a Czech bank was found despite searching in Czech using native case-study vocabulary ('případová studie', 'reference', 'implementace').

result.result_summary: cs-language search surfaced other vendors' CZ bank case studies (Salesforce via Enehano, MS Dynamics via LLP CRM) but nothing from Comarch.

why_it_matters: Comarch's CZ banking footprint may be insurance/telco-weighted rather than banking; needs a direct crawl of comarch.com/cz case studies to confirm.

description: NCR Atleos: CZ appears only inside multi-country lists (contactless ATM availability, ATMaaS coverage), with no dedicated CZ bank announcement located.

result.result_summary: Country-list mentions confirmed presence; no named CZ counterparty.

why_it_matters: Presence without a named client is a strong signal that the CZ relationship is either via a processor/ITCARD-style intermediary or contractually confidential.

description: All URLs in this slice are provided as discovered from search-result metadata and content summaries; no liveness claim is made for any of them.

result.result_summary: Pending deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Several are deep IR permalinks (Diebold Nixdorf /default.aspx, Euronet gcs-web mirrors) that are prone to redirect or path changes without being dead.

description: Most global vendors in this cell publish CZ-relevant material only in English; Czech-language vendor-owned content was found almost exclusively from CEE-headquartered vendors (Asseco) and local SIs.

result.result_summary: cs-language queries were productive for local SIs and Asseco, unproductive for Temenos/Backbase/ACI/Nexi.

why_it_matters: Collection strategy must be split: English crawls for global vendor newsrooms, Czech crawls for local SI/partner reference pages.

description: STRV (CZ/US product studio) and Cetin / T-Mobile ICT services were named in the cell brief but no banking-sector reference, case study or client page for them surfaced in either Czech or English searches in this pass.

result.result_summary: No STRV banking case study and no CZ telco-ICT banking reference page located; only generic corporate pages appeared. Treat as not-yet-found, not as absent.

why_it_matters: Leaves a hole in the boutique-studio and telco-ICT delivery channels, both of which can hold bank digital-channel and infrastructure contracts.

description: The Czech phrase 'reference' and 'případová studie' are extremely noisy — searches for integrator+bank case studies return unrelated CRM vendors, moving companies (Stěhování KB), document-archiving vendors and student theses.

result.result_summary: Multiple queries returned mostly off-target domains (llpcrm.com, awigo.cz, easyproject.com, scribd copies) rather than the target integrators' own sites.

why_it_matters: Recurring collection must query vendor domains directly (site-scoped) rather than relying on open web search, or precision will stay low.

description: Cleverlance Enterprise Solutions' own reference/case-study page URL was not directly surfaced; evidence of its bank work (multichannel banking, Česká spořitelna application design) came only via third-party press and encyclopaedia entries.

result.result_summary: Bank work is evidenced but the canonical vendor reference page was not identified in this pass; its content may now sit under the Aricoma domain after the group rebranding.

why_it_matters: Cleverlance is one of the largest CZ suppliers of bank multichannel systems; missing its primary reference page understates the competitive picture.

description: No pass was made over LinkedIn company/employee pages, GitHub/technology-partner directories (e.g. Camunda, Temenos, Backbase, Microsoft partner finders) which list CZ implementation partners for named bank platforms.

result.result_summary: Not searched in this run.

why_it_matters: OEM partner directories are among the highest-yield pointer sources for identifying which CZ integrator implements which banking product.

description: or.justice.cz sbírka listin document retrieval typically requires session-bound navigation and serves scanned PDFs; automation feasibility was not tested here.

result.result_summary: URL and mechanism identified from documentation; no fetch attempted, so accessibility is a hypothesis.

why_it_matters: The registry is the highest-credibility source in this cell; if the UI resists automation the dataor.justice.cz bulk feed or a mirror must carry the load.

description: Czech-language searches for GoPay partnership press releases returned only help-centre documentation and blog posts; no dedicated 'tiskové zprávy' / press-release section for GoPay was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: GoPay appears to communicate partnerships through its blog rather than a formal newsroom; partnership announcements must be reconstructed from blog posts and third-party media.

why_it_matters: Collection design for GoPay must target the blog and ČTK wire rather than an expected /press endpoint, otherwise partnership events will be missed.

description: Czech-language searching for ThePay, Barion CZ, Adyen CZ, Stripe CZ and Revolut Business CZ returned mostly third-party integration help pages (webczech, wpjshop, Dativery) rather than the vendors' own Czech-market communications.

result.result_summary: No CZ-localized newsroom or country page was surfaced for Adyen, Stripe, Barion or Revolut in this pass; Revolut in particular did not appear in softPOS/terminal supplier results for CZ.

why_it_matters: The international-entrant leg of the cell is currently evidenced only indirectly. Their CZ presence may have to be tracked via the ČNB/JERRS register, EU passporting notifications and merchant-side integration docs rather than vendor PR.

description: KB SmartPay and Visa CZ newsroom entry URLs were inferred from brand names and third-party references rather than confirmed by fetching the pages during this pass.

description: No public, enumerable registry of Bank iD RELYING PARTIES (poskytovatelé služeb / SeP) was located. Searches surfaced only the member-bank list, the implementation page, and scattered individual announcements; secondary sources explicitly advise checking the operator's own site for the current list, implying no downloadable roster.

description: Czech-language searching for ČNB public procurement / supplier information for CERTIS and the instant-payment platform returned only scheme documentation, no tender notices, contract awards or supplier names.

description: The COBS rulebook PDF referenced by search results (cbaonline.cz/upload/1061-cobs-rulebook-v04-1-1.pdf) and references to later versions (v2, v6.0) could not be reconciled to a canonical version index; the ČBA landing page fetched exposed no version numbers, working groups or download links.

why_it_matters: Without a canonical COBS version index we cannot date standard changes, which is the mechanism that links regulation to bank IT spend.

description: No search was run in Czech for CERTIS/instant-payments ISO 20022 migration terminology or for ČNB annual payment-system reports (Zpráva o platebním styku), so those sub-areas are undocumented in this slice.

description: The cell brief lists 'Bankovnictví.cz' and 'Zdroj' as outlets. description: No Reuters or Bloomberg dedicated stream for Czech bank technology/vendor contracts was found. Searches for Reuters coverage of Komerční banka technology contracts returned only stock-data aggregators (MarketBeat, TradingView, SimplyWallSt) and Wikipedia, not wire reporting.

description: No Celent, Forrester or Gartner report specifically sizing Czech banking/payments vendor market share was located. Celent's European e-commerce payments modelling covers DE, NL, PL, ES and UK — Czechia is explicitly not in that set.

description: The Czech-language seed query about foreign media reporting Czech bank technology contracts ('zahraniční média česká banka technologická smlouva oznámení dodavatel') returned only ČNB regulatory opinions and ČNB e-ZAK procurement documents — no meta-coverage of foreign reporting.

why_it_matters: Documents a method correction: for this English-language cell, local-language value comes from local entity names and aliases, not from local phrasing about foreign media.

description: Several high-value sources in this cell (bne IntelliNews, Euromoney, American Banker/PaymentsSource, Celent, Gartner/Forrester, GlobalData) are metered or subscription-only; full-text confirmation of deal details was not possible from search results alone.

why_it_matters: Budget or licence decisions are needed before these sources can be relied on for evidence rather than signal detection.
